not_built: The kit supports the chamber features none, columns and crystal; a `pool` feature is refused by the generator until its water has a spawn-block policy entry (K4, The Strait Grotto, therefore has a dry chamber: its Tapu Fini and Nihilego spawn from the Habitat Block's pool on the grounded floor, which is unmeasured for water-typed species, HB-1). A rare-spawn chamber may host a second ultra-rare beast (`occupant.co_occupants`, K4's Nihilego), which the generator and the audit check as an ultra-rare entry of the chamber pool. Passages are straight (no `turn`): a cave is one axis from its mouth to its chamber. Natural-style Habitat Blocks in the passages are not emitted; only activated blocks (HB-1 and RS-1 are unmeasured). Passages of a kitted cave are straight; only a natural cave winds (`bend`), and its walls carry ore (`dressing.vein_one_in`), its floor patches (`dressing.patch_one_in`) and its hall `knobs`

geometry.rules: A cave is entered at its `mouth.anchor` (the middle column of the mouth) from its `mouth.front` (tools/mines.py frame(): north means the player stands north and the passage runs +z; south runs -z; west runs +x; east runs -x; u runs across, +x on a north or south front and +z on a west or east one; d runs into the hill, d = 0 is the mouth line). The mouth floor y0 is the lower median of the heightmap's ground (tools/ground.py, rounded) over row d = -1, u = -(hw+1) .. hw+1, where hw is the first passage's half width. Rows, in order: d = 0 the mouth (floor y0; timber posts at u = +-(hw+1) from y0+1 to y0+H and a beam of timber over u = -(hw+1) .. hw+1 at y0+H+1, H the first passage's height; one hanging lantern under the beam at u = 0); then the `passages` one after another, the first an `incline` of `length` = drop rows d = 1 .. drop, row d with floor top ft = y0 - d + 1 (a stair block facing the mouth's side, as the mining caves), the later ones level `drift` or `crawl` rows at yh = y0 - drop; then the `antechamber` if any (a room of half width `half_width`, `length` rows, `height`), then, if the cave has a gate, the door row (one row, half width door_half_width, height door_height, filled with barrier blocks over its whole cross-section) and `link_rows` rows of drift at half width door_half_width; then the oval `chamber`: centred on u = 0 at row dc = (its first row) + rz, a cell (u, d) is inside when u*u*rz*rz + (d-dc)^2*rx*rx <= rx*rx*rz*rz, air from yh+1 to yh+h over a floor at yh. Every row of a passage, link or room is air from its floor top + 1 to its floor top + height over u = -hw .. hw (the room's half width); an incline row whose least ground over u = -(hw+1) .. hw+1 is under its air top + 1 + cover_min.passage is an open cutting (air up to the higher of the ground and the air top, plus clear_above), every other row, and every room, must be a tunnel: ground over its air top >= the cover_min of its kind (passage 3, room 4). At most max_cutting_rows rows are cuttings. Shell: every non-air cell in the same column hull that lies within `margin` (passage 2, room 3, cutting 1) in x and z of an air column, from the lowest air cell minus the margin to the highest air cell plus the margin, is the cave's shell block, but only at or under ground - 1 (at or under ground next to a cutting). Wherever an air column's floor is more than one block over the ground, the cells from ground + 1 up to the floor (under a stair, under a floor, under a mouth post) are `fill` of the shell block, at most max_fill deep; the mouth's posts stand on such fill the same way. Lanterns stand on posts (a spruce fence block with a standing lantern on it, never a light block): on every row d of a level passage with (d - the passage's first row) % lantern_every == lantern_every // 2, alternately on the left and right wall column (u = -hw first, then +hw, counting across the whole cave), on the antechamber's two end corners (u = +-(half_width - 1) at its last row minus one), and four in the chamber at u = +-round(0.6 rx), d = dc +- round(0.55 rz). A chamber feature `columns` puts two full-height columns (the cave's column block) at u = +-round(0.5 rx), d = dc; `crystal` stands amethyst clusters (facing up) on the floor at the chamber cells the hash h32(seed, sid(cave id), u, d) orders first (tools/mines.py's mix; ties by (u, d)), `crystal_count` of them, skipping lantern posts and any cell with (u/rx)^2 + ((d-dc)/rz)^2 under 0.16. Rounding is Python's round(). The Habitat Block of a part replaces the floor cell at that part's centre (the chamber's centre; the antechamber's middle). NATURAL CAVES (`mode` "natural"; the owner, 2026-10-12: 'we need caves on Northlight, Long Isle and Sunset. They don't have to go anywhere or have a reward; just a cave would seem natural'). A natural cave has no gate, occupant, antechamber, Habitat Block, reward or keeper, and it writes no timber frame, no fence post, no lantern and no column: its mouth is the rock's own opening (no posts, no beam, no hanging lantern; the mouth-floor, apron, cutting and cover rules above are unchanged) and it is dark by design (lanterns are never written). Its later passages may WIND: a passage with an integer `bend` b (|b| no more than its length, a width of at least 3) puts its row i (0-based, of n rows) on the lateral offset c = c0 + floor((2*b*(i+1) + n) / (2*n)), that is b*(i+1)/n rounded half up, where c0 is the sum of the bends of the passages before it (0 for the mouth and the incline); its air is u = c - hw .. c + hw and the incline does not bend. The chamber is centred on u = uc, the sum of every bend, and a cell (u, d) is inside when (u-uc)^2*rz^2 + (d-dc)^2*rx^2 <= rx^2*rz^2; the shell, floor, fill, cover and cutting rules are otherwise as above, applied to the offset rows. A natural chamber's feature is `none` or `knobs`: `knobs` stands the palette's `knob` block on the floor (yh+1) at the `knob_count` chamber cells the same hash orders first as for `crystal` (u counted across the whole cave, the skip rule (u-uc)^2/rx^2 + (d-dc)^2/rz^2 under 0.16 likewise). DRESSING, once the shell and the knobs are written: every cell of the shell role (not a fill cell) that has an air cell among its six neighbours and whose h32(seed, sid(cave id), x, y, z) is a multiple of the cave's dressing.vein_one_in becomes the palette's `vein` block; every cell of the floor role (the mouth row, the level rows and the chamber, never a stair) whose h32(seed, sid(cave id), x, z, 7) is a multiple of dressing.patch_one_in becomes the palette's `patch` block. A natural cave's palette is shell, floor, stair, vein, patch and knob.

keep_clear.why: tools/mining_caves.py Clearance, reused as it stands (see its docstring): every written column keeps these distances from the town footprints, the routed legs and route paths, the routes' spawn-corridor boxes, every x/z another data file authors (this file, the exempt Habitat Block ids and the exempt files below skipped), every earthwork and placed template, every other built pack's writes, painted water and the water export's changed columns; a surface column keeps tree_reach from a painted tree. authored_clearance is 32 here (12 for the mining caves): a cave is a place, not a gallery. `report` also lists everything within report_radius so the owner can see what is near

authored_exempt.ids: computed by tools/caves.py: every Habitat Block id this file authors (habitat[].id of each cave) is skipped by id in tools/southern_residents.py authored_points, because it stands inside the cave it belongs to; every other Habitat Block in data/habitat_blocks.json stays a keep-clear point

files.world_probes.json: this tool's own presence probes (places.caves in data/world_probes.json) are positions inside the caves

gate.why: legendaries.py's partition pattern (tools/legendaries.py files(): near / open / close): the door opens while a flagged player stands in the antechamber and closes when none does and nobody stands in the door, link or chamber. The driver runs only while somebody is within `reach` of the chamber centre, so whoever trips it holds the chunks it writes

caves.name: Hoarfrost Hollow
caves.role: a natural cave on the south Pine Isle, away from Northlight: nowhere to go and nothing to take
caves.reading: A crack in a spruce hillside that goes down into the cold: the rock sweats frost, the floor is ice in patches and the little hall at the end of the twisting way has blue ice standing in it like teeth. Nothing lives here but the dark.

light.why: a natural cave is left dark: the night is fightorflight's and a dark cave is the right kind of danger (docs/STATE.md); no lantern is ever written
